audit_findings.title: Unfunded pension claims may be missing from the equity bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $41.920 million maximum recorded pension claims: $20.712 million foreign net underfunding plus $21.208 million domestic obligation; $0.70 per diluted share and 3.1% of $1.331 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: A required pension adjustment would reduce the equity bridge, unless the related cash funding is already fully reflected in projected OE; deducting it in both places would double count the claim.
audit_findings.evidence: As of December 28, 2025, the Company had a net liability recorded of $ 20.7 million for the foreign defined benefit plans, an amount equal to their under-funded status, and had recorded in accumulated other comprehensive loss an amount equal to $ 35.3 million (net of taxes of approximately $ 9.1 million) related to the future amounts to be recorded in net periodic benefit costs.
audit_findings.explanation: The omission is not demonstrated because OE retains pension costs and the domestic obligation is partly hedged with company-owned insurance assets. Conservatively deducting both recorded claims would reduce base value from $22.19 to about $21.49 per share, still far below the $37.24 market price and leaving the valuation conclusion unchanged. The $35.3 million after-tax actuarial loss in AOCI is not an additional liability beyond the recorded funded-status amounts.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile the disclosed $34.228 million pension cash obligations and projected contributions or benefit payments to pension expense retained in OE; then rerun the bridge for only the claim not captured in OE, net of tax effects and genuinely available insurance assets.

audit_findings.title: The bridge may treat operating cash as distributable excess cash
audit_findings.magnitude: $81.528 million maximum bridge exposure; $1.36 per diluted share and 6.1% of $1.331 billion base equity value
audit_findings.mechanism: Minimum operating cash, locally required balances, and repatriation taxes would reduce the cash-and-short-term-investments addition in the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We consider cash located outside of the U.S. as indefinitely reinvested in the respective jurisdictions (except as identified below).
audit_findings.explanation: The distributability assumption is unresolved, but even removing the entire latest cash balance—an upper bound exceeding any operating-cash or tax haircut—would reduce base value from $22.19 to about $20.83 per share and bull value from $25.94 to about $24.58. Both remain well below the $37.24 market price, so this cannot change the present valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain the July 5, 2026 cash balance by jurisdiction, determine minimum operating cash, and calculate applicable withholding and state taxes; rerun the bridge with only verified excess cash.

audit_findings.title: Finance-lease principal may escape the owner-earnings calculation
audit_findings.magnitude: $3.059 million of 2025 finance-lease principal; if entirely recurring and omitted, approximately $43.0 million of base value, $0.72 per diluted share, using the computed $1,250 million/$89 million base operating-PV multiple
audit_findings.mechanism: Adding back finance-lease asset amortization through D&A while excluding principal payments and noncash leased-asset additions from capital expenditure would overstate OE.
audit_findings.evidence: The Company has operating and finance leases for manufacturing equipment, corporate offices, showrooms, vehicles, distribution facilities, design centers, as well as computer and office equipment.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting mismatch is possible but not demonstrated because the supplied record does not show the calculator's D&A and maintenance-capex components. Even assuming all $3.059 million of 2025 principal was recurring and omitted would reduce base value by only about 3.2%, from $22.19 to approximately $21.47 per share, without changing the conclusion relative to the $37.24 price.
audit_findings.action: Trace the $3.477 million 2025 finance-lease amortization, $3.059 million principal payments, and $3.978 million noncash leased-asset additions through the OE calculation; rerun OE by either excluding the amortization add-back or deducting the corresponding sustaining lease investment, without double counting interest.

audit_findings.title: The PFAS lawsuit is an unquantified claim ahead of common equity
audit_findings.mechanism: Uninsured defense, settlement, judgment, or remediation payments would reduce future OE or require a contingent-liability deduction from the equity bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: We cannot at this time estimate the reasonably possible loss or range of loss, if any, for this matter.
audit_findings.explanation: The lawsuit and absence of a valuation adjustment are demonstrated, but the filing states that no reasonably possible loss or range can be estimated. The latest 10-Q reports no material change. Because PFAS litigation can produce costs outside historical OE and the record supplies no defensible upper bound, materiality cannot presently be established or dismissed.
audit_findings.action: Review subsequent docket activity, plaintiff-specific exposure evidence, allocation among defendants, insurance limits and exclusions, indemnities, defense-cost accruals, and any newly disclosed loss range; rerun the bridge or OE once an attributable expected cash cost can be supported.

audit_findings.title: Forward sustaining capital needs may exceed the historical charge embedded in OE
audit_findings.magnitude: $55 million planned 2026 capital expenditures, $8.808 million above 2025 filed cash capital expenditures of $46.192 million; maintenance portion unquantified
audit_findings.mechanism: Any recurring maintenance, compliance, or finance-lease-funded investment above the amount deducted in the OE anchor would reduce OE before applying growth and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: We estimate aggregate capital expenditures in 2026 to be approximately $55 million, although we are not committed to this amount.
audit_findings.explanation: The $55 million amount is forward-looking and explicitly not committed. The record does not classify it between sustaining and expansion investment, so it does not demonstrate an error in the historical OE series. The $8.808 million increase over 2025 capex is a monitoring indicator, not a supportable OE adjustment, particularly because the filing attributes recent investment to automation and robotics that may be growth or productivity capital.
audit_findings.action: Compare full-year 2026 cash capex and noncash finance-lease additions with the $55 million plan, classify projects as maintenance, compliance, or expansion, and rerun the anchor and scenarios if recurring sustaining investment exceeds the maintenance-capex charge already embedded in OE.
